facts.text: It happens every time I go from lying down to sitting up.
I can't sit or stand without briefly losing consciousness.
When I sat up here in the emergency department, I felt dizzy just before I passed out.
My vision went blurry just before I passed out.
I yawned just before I passed out.
Yesterday I developed a fever of 39 °C.
I use salbutamol for my asthma.
Apart from asthma, I have no medical problems.
No one in my family has had unexplained fainting.

facts.item: sudden cardiac death in the family
facts.text: No one in my family has died suddenly from a heart problem.

findings.name: heart rate and blood pressure response to sitting up
findings.result: On assuming an upright seated posture, heart rate initially rose to 110 bpm in sinus rhythm with maintained blood pressure; over the next 2–3 minutes it gradually declined to marked sinus bradycardia, at which point he yawned, became dizzy with blurred vision, and lost consciousness.

findings.name: electrocardiogram
findings.result: No PR-interval prolongation and no AV-conduction abnormality.

findings.name: chest CT
findings.result: Bilateral, patchy ground-glass opacities consistent with COVID-19.

findings.name: 24-hour Holter ECG
findings.result: Two sinus pauses of up to 3.4 seconds, episodes of idioventricular rhythm, and a 35-second run of slow ventricular tachycardia.

findings.name: transthoracic echocardiography
findings.result: Normal ventricular size and function without structural abnormalities.

gold.reasoning: 1. Inherited channelopathies (eg, Brugada syndrome) and paroxysmal AV block were considered because of the bradyarrhythmic syncope — “Differential diagnoses in this patient include inherited channelopathies such as Brugada syndrome or paroxysmal AV block.” 2. Structural heart disease was excluded by imaging — “Transthoracic echocardiogram revealed a normal left ventricular ejection fraction without any structural abnormalities.”

leakage.reason: Alias 'syncope' (a gold word) is the clinical name of the presenting symptom itself; the patient text says 'passing out'. The gold adds the mechanism (cardioinhibitory reflex).
Alias 'family history of syncope' uses the gold word for the symptom; the text says 'fainting'.

notes: Index visit: the emergency department presentation after 10 days of syncope on sitting up and 1 day of fever, including the episode observed there (s001–s011).
s013–s015 (Holter, echocardiography, lumbar puncture) were done after ICU admission; they are findings, the Holter with time.

The ED episode (s004) gives both a finding (the monitored sequence) and patient facts (dizziness, blurred vision, yawning that he experienced). The heart rate of 110 bpm in that sequence and the examination heart rate of 107 bpm (s007) are different moments; both are kept.
